title: Genitive Forms: Singular, -i and consonant-ending families review
focus: Retrieve the taught genitive patterns in a mixed review.

exercises.prompt: Recall the singular genitives in order, separated by a comma: bussi (“bus”); hotelli (“hotel”).
exercises.explanation: Keep i and ss: bussi + n = bussin. Keep i and ll: hotelli + n = hotellin.

exercises.prompt: Recall the singular genitives in order, separated by a comma: ovi (“door”); kieli (“language”).
exercises.explanation: Change final i to e: ovi → ove-; add -n to get oven. Change final i to e: kieli → kiele-; add -n to get kielen.

exercises.prompt: Recall the singular genitives in order, separated by a comma: käsi (“hand”); uusi (“new”).
exercises.explanation: Replace -si with -de-: kä + de + n = käden. Replace -si with -de-: uu + de + n = uuden.

exercises.prompt: Recall the singular genitives in order, separated by a comma: puhelin (“phone”); eläin (“animal”).
exercises.explanation: Replace final -in with -ime-: puhel + ime + n = puhelimen. Replace final -in with -ime-: elä + ime + n = eläimen.

exercises.prompt: Recall the singular genitives in order, separated by a comma: vastaus (“answer”); ostos (“purchase”).
exercises.explanation: Replace final s with kse: vastau + kse + n = vastauksen. Replace final s with kse: osto + kse + n = ostoksen.

exercises.prompt: Choose the singular genitives in order: lapsi (“child”); veli (“brother”).
exercises.explanation: Use the stem lapse-: lapsi → lapse-; add -n to get lapsen. Use the stem velje-: veli → velje-; add -n to get veljen.

optionFeedback.lapsen, veljen: Use the stem lapse-: lapsi → lapse-; add -n to get lapsen. Use the stem velje-: veli → velje-; add -n to get veljen.
optionFeedback.lapsi, veljen: Both words need their special singular genitive forms.
optionFeedback.lapsen, veli: Both words need their special singular genitive forms.

exercises.prompt: Recall the singular genitives in order, separated by a comma: taksi (“taxi”); kahvi (“coffee”).
exercises.explanation: Keep i: taksi + n = taksin. Keep i: kahvi + n = kahvin.

exercises.prompt: Recall the singular genitives in order, separated by a comma: nimi (“name”); pieni (“small”).
exercises.explanation: Change final i to e: nimi → nime-; add -n to get nimen. Change final i to e: pieni → piene-; add -n to get pienen.

exercises.prompt: Recall the singular genitives in order, separated by a comma: vesi (“water”); vuosi (“year”).
exercises.explanation: Replace -si with -de-: ve + de + n = veden. Replace -si with -de-: vuo + de + n = vuoden.

exercises.prompt: Recall the singular genitives in order, separated by a comma: avain (“key”); soitin (“instrument”).
exercises.explanation: Replace final -in with -ime-: ava + ime + n = avaimen. Strengthen t to tt and use -ime-: soitin → soittime-; add -n.

exercises.prompt: Recall the singular genitives in order, separated by a comma: kysymys (“question”); kerros (“floor”).
exercises.explanation: Replace final s with kse: kysymy + kse + n = kysymyksen. Replace final s with kse: kerro + kse + n = kerroksen.

exercises.prompt: Choose the singular genitives in order: mies (“man”); poika (“boy”).
exercises.explanation: Use the special stem miehe-: mies → miehe-; add -n to get miehen. Use the weak stem poja-: poika → poja-; add -n to get pojan.

optionFeedback.miehen, pojan: Use the special stem miehe-: mies → miehe-; add -n to get miehen. Use the weak stem poja-: poika → poja-; add -n to get pojan.
optionFeedback.mies, pojan: Both words need their special singular genitive forms.
optionFeedback.miehen, poika: Both words need their special singular genitive forms.

exercises.prompt: Recall the singular genitives in order, separated by a comma: hotelli (“hotel”); posti (“post”).
exercises.explanation: Keep i and ll: hotelli + n = hotellin. Keep i: posti + n = postin.

exercises.prompt: Recall the singular genitives in order, separated by a comma: kieli (“language”); suuri (“large”).
exercises.explanation: Change final i to e: kieli → kiele-; add -n to get kielen. Change final i to e: suuri → suure-; add -n to get suuren.

exercises.prompt: Recall the singular genitives in order, separated by a comma: uusi (“new”); kuusi (“six”).
exercises.explanation: Replace -si with -de-: uu + de + n = uuden. For the number six, replace -si with -de-: kuu + de + n = kuuden. The tree word kuusi has a different stem.

exercises.prompt: Recall the singular genitives in order, separated by a comma: eläin (“animal”); keitin (“brewing device”).
exercises.explanation: Replace final -in with -ime-: elä + ime + n = eläimen. Strengthen t to tt and use -ime-: keitin → keittime-; add -n.

exercises.prompt: Recall the singular genitives in order, separated by a comma: ostos (“purchase”); keskus (“centre”).
exercises.explanation: Replace final s with kse: osto + kse + n = ostoksen. Replace final s with kse: kesku + kse + n = keskuksen.

exercises.prompt: Choose the singular genitives in order: veli (“brother”); lapsi (“child”).
exercises.explanation: Use the stem velje-: veli → velje-; add -n to get veljen. Use the stem lapse-: lapsi → lapse-; add -n to get lapsen.

optionFeedback.veljen, lapsen: Use the stem velje-: veli → velje-; add -n to get veljen. Use the stem lapse-: lapsi → lapse-; add -n to get lapsen.
optionFeedback.veli, lapsen: Both words need their special singular genitive forms.
optionFeedback.veljen, lapsi: Both words need their special singular genitive forms.

exercises.prompt: Recall the singular genitives in order, separated by a comma: kahvi (“coffee”); tiimi (“team”).
exercises.explanation: Keep i: kahvi + n = kahvin. Keep i: tiimi + n = tiimin.

exercises.prompt: Recall the singular genitives in order, separated by a comma: pieni (“small”); saari (“island”).
exercises.explanation: Change final i to e: pieni → piene-; add -n to get pienen. Change final i to e: saari → saare-; add -n to get saaren.

exercises.prompt: Recall the singular genitives in order, separated by a comma: vuosi (“year”); viisi (“five”).
exercises.explanation: Replace -si with -de-: vuo + de + n = vuoden. Replace -si with -de-: vii + de + n = viiden.

exercises.prompt: Recall the singular genitives in order, separated by a comma: soitin (“instrument”); pakastin (“freezer”).
exercises.explanation: Strengthen t to tt and use -ime-: soitin → soittime-; add -n. Replace final -in with -ime-: pakast + ime + n = pakastimen.

exercises.prompt: Recall the singular genitives in order, separated by a comma: kerros (“floor”); päätös (“decision”).
exercises.explanation: Replace final s with kse: kerro + kse + n = kerroksen. Replace final s with kse: päätö + kse + n = päätöksen.

exercises.prompt: Choose the singular genitives in order: poika (“boy”); mies (“man”).
exercises.explanation: Use the weak stem poja-: poika → poja-; add -n to get pojan. Use the special stem miehe-: mies → miehe-; add -n to get miehen.

optionFeedback.pojan, miehen: Use the weak stem poja-: poika → poja-; add -n to get pojan. Use the special stem miehe-: mies → miehe-; add -n to get miehen.
optionFeedback.poika, miehen: Both words need their special singular genitive forms.
